ideas: Ancient cultures, from the Incas to the Greeks, saw mountains as places where heaven and earth meet.
Scholars call this the Cosmic Mountain, a place where the divine and the human intersect.
At Mount Sinai, a newly freed Israel meets God and learns how to live as a new kind of people.
Throughout Scripture, an encounter with God is meant to reshape the way we live.
Matthew places Jesus on seven mountains, and he wants us to notice.
On the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus sits down and teaches like a new Moses … Sinai 2.0.
The Beatitudes announce that God’s kingdom is good news for people who feel overlooked, left behind, or forgotten.
Jesus raises the bar with “love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,” which gets personal quickly.
Knowing better doesn’t automatically mean doing better. The wise builder puts Jesus’ words into practice.
Jesus comes down the mountain, reaches out and touches a man others avoid, and lives what he just taught. What happens up here ought to make a difference down here.
questions: What’s the best view you’ve ever earned by climbing something? Was it worth the effort?
Forrest admitted he’s incredibly patient until someone requires patience and a huge fan of forgiveness until he’s the one who has to forgive. Which of those sounds most like you?

questions.text: . Jesus opens with people who are struggling, grieving, and overlooked. What do you notice about who he starts with? What does that say about who God’s kingdom is for?
. Forrest said it’s easy to pray _about_ people we don’t like and uncomfortable to pray _for_ them. What might change in you if you prayed for someone’s good this week?
. Jesus says the wise builder hears his words and puts them into practice. What’s one thing Jesus said that you admire, agree with, and haven’t started practicing?

questions: After a mountaintop message about mercy, the first person Jesus meets is someone others avoid, and he reaches out and touches him. Who are you tempted to move away from right now, and what would moving toward them look like?
This series hopes to help us encounter God, be changed, and live differently. Which of those three are you most hoping for over the next four weeks?
description: Life gets loud here with deadlines, headlines, and a Monday that keeps introducing you to the person you didn’t plan to be. You know better ... and doing better feels like a steep climb.

In the first week of *Up Here*, Forrest Jenan follows Jesus up a mountain. When Jesus comes back down, he reaches out to the first person he meets. The view from up here has a way of changing what happens down there.
scriptureGroups: Now when Jesus saw the crowds, he went up on a mountainside and sat down. His disciples came to him, and he began to teach them.

for they will inherit the earth.
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness,
for they will be shown mercy.
Blessed are the pure in heart,
for they will be called children of God.
Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness,
for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you and falsely say all kinds of evil against you because of me. Rejoice and be glad, because great is your reward in heaven, for in the same way they persecuted the prophets who were before you.”
